chunks: Those who do not believe in the Hereafter give the angels names of females.
ai.seo_question: Why did the pre-Islamic Arabs call angels 'daughters of God'?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse highlights the pre-Islamic Arabs' tendency to project their own cultural biases onto the divine realm, specifically the Quraysh who associated angels with female deities like Al-Lat and Al-Uzza. This anthropomorphism stems from their denial of the Hereafter, as they could not conceive of a spiritual reality beyond the material world, leading them to treat angels as intercessors or daughters of Allah.
